title: Holding a survey line in current and waves: line-of-sight against integral line-of-sight for a small boat
lede: plain line-of-sight guidance leaves a steady cross-track offset of delta*tan(asin(c/U)) in a cross current c (simulation matches it to 1%: 3.77 m at 0.3 m/s, 12 m look-ahead); integral LOS removes it, with lower rms cross-track error in 136 of 144 cross-current cases and the 8 exceptions all at a 6 m look-ahead with integral gain 2, where it oscillates (rms about 2.3 m even in still water)
summary: Milestone 1 of track 23's marine-path step, filed under the marine-hull programme. A stdlib 3-DOF (surge, sway, yaw) 200 kg boat with a rudder and surge PI, in a constant earth-frame current and a six-sinusoid wave disturbance (4 to 9 s periods, force scale swept, not sourced), follows a straight line under plain LOS and integral LOS (Borhaug, Pavlov and Pettersen 2008). Check: the simulated plain-LOS offset equals the analytic delta*tan(asin(c/U)) to 1% (0.3 m/s, 3.774 m). Sweep: cross current 0 to 0.5 m/s, wave scale 0 to 1, look-ahead 6, 12, 24 m, integral gain 0.5, 1, 2, 3 seeds. Integral LOS has lower rms cross-track error in 136 of 144 cases with current at least 0.2 m/s; the 8 exceptions are all look-ahead 6 m with gain 2, which oscillates. Energy per ground km differs by a median 1.4% (max 37%, in the oscillating cases, which also include the transient). Damping, rudder and wave-force coefficients are not sourced; the model has no Coriolis cross-coupling beyond u*r and v*r, no MPC arm, no JONSWAP spectrum and no field data. Preliminary; simulation only.
